dish: Copycat Taco Bell Quesadilla: Leftover Turkey Edition (12-Minute Speedrun)
caption:
Leftover turkey became crispy copycat Taco Bell quesadillas, $2.42 each.
$16 delivered or $4.85 at home for two, 12 minutes from cold pan.
Ingredients: 150 g leftover turkey, 2 large flour tortillas, 90 g cheddar or mozzarella, 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp pickled jalapeños + 1 tbsp brine, paprika, cumin, garlic powder, 2 tbsp water, 1 tbsp butter.
ingredients: 150 g leftover cooked turkey, shredded (about 1 heaping cup)
90 g block cheddar or mozzarella, shredded (about 1 cup)
steps: Minute 0: In a small bowl stir 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped pickled jalapeños, 1 tbsp jalapeño brine, 1/2 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp cumin and 1/4 tsp garlic powder. That's the copycat Creamy Jalapeño Sauce.

Minute 1: Heat a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium. Add the shredded turkey and 2 tbsp water, cover and steam 3 minutes, stirring once, until steaming hot all the way through (74°C / 165°F). Tip it onto a plate and wipe the pan dry.
Minute 4: Lay out both tortillas. On one half of each, layer a quarter of the cheese, half the turkey, 1 tbsp sauce, then another quarter of the cheese. Fold each tortilla over into a half-moon.

Minute 6: Melt the butter in the same skillet over medium. Add both folded quesadillas side by side, straight edges in the middle. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, pressing with a spatula, until deep golden underneath.
Minute 9: Flip both. Cook 2 more minutes until golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Minute 11: Slide onto a board, rest 30 seconds, cut each into 3 wedges and serve with the leftover sauce for dipping. Timer stops at 12:00.

dish: Crispy Leftover Stuffing Waffles with Turkey, Gravy and Cranberry
caption:
Leftover stuffing became crispy stuffing waffles with turkey, gravy and cranberry, $2.16 a serving.
The waffle iron hack: does it stick or release? Rated honestly. $4.32 total, serves 2, 25 minutes.

Ingredients: 2 cups leftover stuffing, 1 egg, 2 tbsp milk, 1 cup leftover turkey, 1/2 cup gravy, 1/4 cup cranberry sauce, 1 tsp canola oil
ingredients: 120 g (about 1 cup) Leftover cooked turkey, sliced or shredded
steps: 1. Preheat your waffle iron to medium-high. No waffle iron? Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat instead.
2. Put the stuffing in a mixing bowl and break up any big clumps with a fork.
3. In a small bowl, beat the egg with the milk, then stir it into the stuffing until it holds together when squeezed. If it still feels crumbly, add another splash of milk.
4. Brush the waffle iron lightly with oil. Pack in half the stuffing mixture and close the lid.
5. Cook 6 to 8 minutes without opening early, until deep golden and crisp. The centre should reach 74°C / 165°F on a thermometer, since it contains raw egg and leftovers.

6. Lift the waffle out with a spatula and keep it warm on a plate. Repeat with the rest of the mixture. (Skillet method: press the mixture into two 1.5 cm thick patties and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until crisp and 74°C / 165°F inside.)
7. While the waffles cook, put the gravy in a saucepan and bring it to a gentle boil, stirring.
8. Add the turkey to the gravy, cover, and heat on low for 3 to 5 minutes until the turkey is steaming hot, 74°C / 165°F.
9. Plate each waffle, spoon the turkey and gravy over the top, and finish with a dollop of cranberry sauce.

dish: Copycat KFC Famous Bowl: Leftover Turkey Edition (Popcorn Turkey, Mash, Corn, Gravy & Cheese)
caption:
Leftover turkey, cold mash and half a can of corn just became crunchy popcorn turkey Famous Bowls. 🍗
Copycat KFC Famous Bowl for two in 18 minutes, $4.91 total ($2.46 a bowl).
Ingredients: leftover turkey, flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, 1 egg, vegetable oil, leftover mashed potatoes, canned corn, turkey gravy, cheddar.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 mL) vegetable oil, for shallow frying
150 g (about 1 1/2 cups) leftover cooked turkey, cut into 2 cm popcorn-size chunks
1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper
1/2 can (about 3/4 cup drained) canned corn, from a 341 mL can
1/2 cup (50 g) shredded cheddar, from a block
steps: Pour the oil into a 25 cm (10-inch) skillet. It should sit about 5 mm deep. Heat over medium-high for about 4 minutes, until it reaches 175°C (350°F) or a pinch of flour sizzles right away.

While the oil heats, mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper in a bowl. Toss the turkey chunks in the seasoned flour, dip them in the beaten egg, then toss them in the flour again. Let them sit on a plate for 2 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat each leftover in its own covered microwave-safe bowl. Give the mashed potatoes about 3 minutes and stir halfway, adding a splash of milk or water if they're stiff. Drain the corn and give it about 1 minute. Heat the gravy for about 2 minutes, stirring once, until it is bubbling. All leftovers must be steaming hot, 74°C (165°F).

Fry the turkey in a single layer for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes per side, until deep golden and crisp. The turkey is already cooked, so you are only crisping the coating and heating it through to 74°C (165°F). Drain on a paper towel.

Build two bowls. Start with a cup of hot mash in each, then add a spoonful of corn and the popcorn turkey. Pour the hot gravy over everything and finish with the cheddar. The heat from the gravy melts the cheese in about 30 seconds. Serve right away.

dish: Leftover Mashed Potato Korokke Hand Rolls (Crispy Potato Croquette Temaki with Spicy Mayo)
caption:
Cold leftover mash → shatter-crisp croquettes rolled in nori. 🥔🍙
8 hand rolls, $4.85 total, $1.21 a serving, 20 minutes.
Ingredients: leftover mashed potatoes, flour, egg, panko, oil, leftover rice, rice vinegar, sugar, salt, nori, cucumber, mayo, sriracha, soy sauce.
ingredients: 2 cups cold leftover mashed potatoes (about 400 g potatoes' worth, already made with butter and milk)
2 tbsp all-purpose flour, plus extra if the mash is very soft
1/2 cup vegetable oil, for shallow frying
2 cups cold cooked white rice (leftover, refrigerated no more than 3 days; short-grain is stickiest if you have it)
4 sheets nori, cut in half (8 half-sheets)
steps: Shape the croquettes (3 min): Take the mash straight from the fridge. If it feels sticky or loose, work in 1 to 2 extra tbsp flour. Roll it into 8 finger-shaped logs about 10 cm long and 2 cm thick.
Bread them (2 min): Put the 2 tbsp flour, the beaten egg and the panko in three shallow bowls. Roll each log in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.

Fry (7 min): Heat the 1/2 cup oil in a large skillet over medium-high to about 350°F (175°C), until a panko crumb sizzles immediately. Fry the logs, turning every 1.5 to 2 minutes, for 6 to 7 minutes total until deep golden on all sides and steaming hot in the center (74°C/165°F). Drain on paper towel.

Season the rice while they fry (3 min): Microwave the rice with 1 tbsp water, covered, for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through. Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt together until dissolved, then fold into the rice with a cutting motion and spread it on a plate to cool to warm.
Mix the spicy mayo (30 sec): Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together. Add more sriracha if you like it hotter.

Roll and eat (3 min): Lay a half-sheet of nori shiny side down in your palm. Press about 1/4 cup rice onto the left third. Lay a croquette and a few cucumber sticks diagonally across the rice and drizzle with spicy mayo. Fold the bottom-left corner up over the filling and roll into a cone. Serve right away with soy sauce for dipping, while the nori and panko are still crisp.

caption:
Delivery fried rice: $18 and 45 minutes. Mine: $4.80 and 20 minutes, with leftover turkey.
The trick? Dry the rice so it fries instead of steams.
Rice, oil, onion, garlic, frozen mixed veg, leftover turkey, 2 eggs, soy sauce, pepper.
ingredients: 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) water plus a pinch of salt
1 cup (120 g) frozen mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, corn)
1 cup (120 g) leftover roast turkey, shredded bite-size (refrigerated no more than 3-4 days)
2 large eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a small pot with 300 ml water and a pinch of salt, then bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat, rest it covered for 2 minutes, then spread it on a large plate or sheet pan to steam off while you prep.
While the rice cooks, dice the onion, mince the garlic, shred the turkey into bite-size pieces and beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until it shimmers. Cook the onion for 2 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the frozen vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes until hot and any water has cooked off.
Push the vegetables to one side and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the empty side. Pour in the eggs and scramble for 30-45 seconds until just set, then break them up into the vegetables.

Add the rice and turkey. Press everything flat, let it sit for 1 minute to toast, then toss. Repeat for 3-4 minutes until the rice crackles and the turkey is steaming hot all the way through (74°C/165°F).
Drizzle the soy sauce around the hot edge of the pan, add the pepper and toss for 30 seconds. Taste, adjust the salt and serve immediately.

dish: $5 Leftover Turkey Monte Cristo (Brunch-Diner Copycat with Cranberry Dip)
caption:
Two brunch Monte Cristos ran me $50. This one's $4.75 for two, and it uses your Thanksgiving turkey.
Lid on, medium-low, 15 minutes. Tart cranberry dip > sugary jam.
You need: 2 eggs, 1/4 cup milk, pinch of salt, 1 tsp Dijon, 4 slices white bread, 2 slices Swiss, 3 oz leftover turkey, 1.5 oz deli ham, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tsp powdered sugar, 2 tbsp cranberry sauce
ingredients: 3 oz leftover roast turkey, sliced (refrigerated no more than 3-4 days, thawed from frozen, or deli turkey)
2 tbsp leftover cranberry sauce, warmed, for dipping
steps: In a shallow dish, whisk the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt until no streaks of white remain.
Build 2 sandwiches. Spread Dijon on 2 slices of bread. Layer 1 slice of Swiss, half the turkey and half the ham on each, then top with the remaining bread and press down gently.
Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Dip each sandwich into the egg mixture for about 5 seconds per side, letting the excess drip off.

Cook the sandwiches covered with a lid for 3-4 minutes, until the bottoms are deep golden. Flip, cover again, and cook another 3-4 minutes. They're ready when the cheese is fully melted and the center is steaming hot (165°F/74°C on an instant-read thermometer).
While the second side cooks, warm the cranberry sauce in the microwave for 20-30 seconds and stir until loose.
Cut each sandwich in half diagonally, dust with powdered sugar, and serve right away with the warm cranberry sauce for dipping.

dish: Budget Susur Lee-Style Singapore Slaw (Cranberry 'Plum' Dressing Copycat)
caption:
Stop drowning your slaw before it hits the table. 🥗
Toronto's famous Singapore Slaw copycat for $4.79 total ($1.20 a serving) in 15 minutes, with cranberry sauce as the plum sauce.
Ingredients: cabbage, carrot, cucumber, red onion, rice vinegar, instant ramen, peanuts, sesame seeds, cranberry sauce, soy sauce, lime, vegetable oil, sesame oil, chili flakes, green onions
ingredients: 1/2 small red onion, very thinly sliced
1/4 small green cabbage (about 300 g), finely shredded
1 medium carrot, julienned or coarsely grated
1/4 English cucumber, seeded and cut into thin matchsticks
1 package instant ramen noodles (seasoning packet set aside for another use)
1/3 cup leftover or canned cranberry sauce (whole-berry or jellied)
steps: Quick-pickle first: in a small bowl, stir 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt until dissolved. Add the thinly sliced red onion, press it under the liquid and let it sit for 10 minutes while you prep everything else.

Shred the cabbage as finely as you can, julienne or grate the carrot, and cut the seeded cucumber into thin matchsticks. Pat the cucumber dry with a paper towel, then pile all the vegetables into a large bowl and refrigerate them, undressed.

Make the crunch: crush the ramen block into small pieces, still inside the bag. Toast in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring often, until golden and fragrant. Add the sesame seeds for the last 30 to 60 seconds, until lightly golden. Tip onto a plate to cool, then mix in the chopped peanuts.

Whisk the dressing: mash 1/3 cup cranberry sauce with a fork until mostly smooth. Whisk in 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp of the onion pickling liquid, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp sesame oil and a pinch of chili flakes. Taste it; it should be sweet, salty and tangy, like plum sauce.
Right before serving (not a minute sooner), drain the pickled onions and scatter them over the cold vegetables with the green onions. Pour on the dressing and toss well for about 30 seconds.
Shower the toasted noodle, peanut and sesame crunch over the top, give it one last quick toss, and serve immediately while it is loud and crunchy.

dish: Copycat Olive Garden Pasta e Fagioli (One-Pot, 20-Minute Speedrun)
caption:
Olive Garden's pasta e fagioli, copycat style, in one pot and 20 real minutes.
Cook the pasta IN the soup and mash a few beans: thick broth, no cream.
$4.41 for 4 bowls, $1.10 each.

Oil, onion, carrot, celery, garlic, Italian seasoning, crushed tomatoes, water, bouillon, ditalini, kidney beans, parmesan, salt & pepper
ingredients: 1 L (4 cups) water, boiled in the kettle
1 can (540 mL) red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
10 g (2 tbsp) grated parmesan, for serving
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Minute 0: Start the kettle with 1 L water. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high. Dice the onion, carrot and celery and add them to the pot as you go. Cook, stirring, until the onion softens, about 4 minutes total.

Minute 4: Add the garlic and Italian seasoning and stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the crushed tomatoes, the hot kettle water and the bouillon cubes. Cover and bring to a full boil, about 2 minutes.

Minute 7: Uncover. Add the ditalini and the drained, rinsed beans. Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot with your spoon. Simmer uncovered at a lively bubble for 9 to 10 minutes, stirring every minute so the pasta doesn't stick, until the ditalini is tender.
Minute 17: Taste. Season with salt and pepper. If it's thicker than you like, add a splash of hot water.

Minute 19: Ladle into four bowls and top each with parmesan. Serve right away. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 to 4 days. The pasta keeps drinking the broth, so add water when reheating, and reheat until steaming hot.

dish: Copycat Panera Mac & Cheese (One-Pot, No-Roux Evaporated Milk Hack)
caption:
Copycat Panera mac & cheese with NO flour, NO butter, NO roux. One pot, 15 minutes, $2.06 a bowl. I tried to break the sauce and it stayed glossy. Score: 9/10.

Ingredients: 170 g medium pasta shells, ~500 mL water, 1/2 tsp salt, 170 mL evaporated milk (half a can), 170 g old white cheddar (grated from the block), 1/2 tsp Dijon, 3-4 dashes hot sauce, black pepper
ingredients: About 500 mL (2 cups) cold water, enough to just cover the pasta
170 mL (about 3/4 cup, half a 354 mL can) evaporated milk
170 g (6 oz) old white cheddar, grated from the block (about 2 cups loosely packed)
steps: Grate the cheddar off the block and set it aside. Measure out the evaporated milk.
Put the shells in a small saucepan with the salt. Add cold water just until the pasta is barely covered, about 500 mL (2 cups).

Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower to medium-high. Stir every 30 seconds so the shells don't stick, about 7-9 minutes, until the pasta is al dente and nearly all the water is absorbed. Leave about 2-3 tablespoons of starchy liquid in the pot. If it runs dry before the pasta is tender, add a splash of water.
Pour in the evaporated milk and bring it to a bare simmer, about 1 minute.
Turn the heat to low. Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring constantly until each handful melts, about 1-2 minutes total. Don't let it boil once the cheese is in.
Off the heat, stir in the Dijon, hot sauce and black pepper. If it's thick, loosen it with a splash of evaporated milk or water. Rest 1 minute so the sauce clings, then serve right away.

dish: One Box of Spaghetti, 3 Ways: Copycat Panda Express Chow Mein, Garlic Noodles and Aglio e Olio
caption:
Copycat Panda Express chow mein, garlic noodles AND aglio e olio, all from one $1.20 box of spaghetti. Three dinners, $3.40 total, $1.13 a plate.
You need: 1 lb spaghetti, cabbage, soy sauce, butter, garlic, oyster sauce, olive oil, chili flakes.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon kosher salt for the pasta water (pantry)
10 garlic cloves total (6 minced, 4 thinly sliced)
steps: Bring 4 quarts of water and 1 tablespoon of salt to a rolling boil in a large stock pot. Cook 1 lb spaghetti for 9 minutes, until just al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, drain, and divide the noodles into three portions.
Chow mein: heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 cups of shredded cabbage and cook 2 to 3 minutes until wilted with golden edges.
Add one portion of spaghetti and 2 tablespoons of soy sauce. Toss with tongs for 2 minutes until the noodles are glazed and lightly browned. Plate and wipe out the skillet.
Garlic noodles: melt 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat, add 6 minced garlic cloves and cook 1 minute until fragrant, not brown. Stir in 1 tablespoon of oyster sauce.
Add the second portion of spaghetti plus 2 tablespoons of pasta water and toss 1 minute until glossy. Plate and wipe out the skillet.
Aglio e olio: warm 3 tablespoons of olive oil over medium-low heat with 4 thinly sliced garlic cloves for 2 to 3 minutes until pale gold. Add 1/2 teaspoon chili flakes for 15 seconds.
Add the last portion of spaghetti and 1/4 cup of pasta water. Toss vigorously for 1 minute until the oil and water emulsify into a silky sauce. Serve all three hot.

dish: Copycat Olive Garden Fettuccine Alfredo (Pantry Version)
caption:
Copycat Olive Garden Fettuccine Alfredo for $4.50 total. You probably have everything for this right now.
The trick: cheese goes in OFF the heat so it stays silky.
Fettuccine, butter, garlic, flour, milk, parmesan, black pepper.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add 1 tablespoon salt and the fettuccine. Cook 1 minute less than package time, about 9-10 minutes.
While pasta cooks, melt 3 tablespoons butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant, not browned.
Whisk in 1 tablespoon flour and cook 30 seconds. Slowly whisk in 1 1/2 cups milk and simmer 3-4 minutes, whisking, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the skillet off the heat and let it sit 30 seconds. Whisk in the parmesan a handful at a time until smooth (too much heat makes the cheese grainy).
Use tongs to move the pasta straight into the sauce with about 1/4 cup pasta water. Toss over low heat 1 minute until glossy, adding more pasta water as needed.
Season with black pepper and a pinch of salt to taste. Serve immediately with extra parmesan.

caption:
The $34 restaurant spicy rigatoni... for $4.94 a pot. That's $1.24 a plate, and honestly? Budget wins.
Rigatoni, butter, onion, garlic, tomato paste, chili flakes, vodka, heavy cream, parmesan, pasta water.
steps: Salt your water like the sea and drop one pound of rigatoni. Pull it one minute early.
Meanwhile, two tablespoons butter, half a diced onion, two cloves of garlic. Soft and sweet, not brown.
Quarter cup of tomato paste. Fry it till brick red, because caramelized sugars are the whole restaurant secret.
One teaspoon chili flakes, then two tablespoons of vodka. Hear that hiss? The alcohol cooks off and wakes up the tomato.
Half a cup of heavy cream. Stir and watch it go blush pink and silky.
Rigatoni in with a splash of starchy pasta water. That starch glues sauce to every ridge.
Half a cup of parmesan, off the heat so it melts instead of clumping. Wait for that gloss.
Honestly? I'd put this up against the thirty-four dollar plate any night. Spicy, creamy, every tube filled.
Total, four dollars ninety-four. Four plates, about a dollar twenty-four each. Verdict: budget wins, no contest.
